name: concepts-readroom/b-full-c
refs: THE LAYOUT (a flat wireframe, project-owned): where things go on the 1024x600 game screen (the screen is centred in this 16:9 canvas). A dark top bar and a dark bottom line; the wall behind; the table top from a little above the middle down; a brass lamp over the pod; the pod on its dish in the lamp's pool; the creature to its right; small pinned papers top left (a photo and a slip) and top right (a card). The bottom of the table is left empty. Take only the placement and the sizes. Never copy its flat look, and paint no lines, arcs or boxes from it.

THE ROOM'S MATERIALS (our signed reading-room bench painting, project-owned): its umber wood, cream plaster wall, the small low brass lamp and its warm pool of light. The new picture is clearly made by the same hand, but at night: the wall goes to soft shadow away from the lamp.

THE POD (project-owned game art): our Loika pod, an upright seed pod with a round coral cap, slate-blue body, pale vertical ribs and coral dots. Keep its shape, cap, ribs and dots; it is the hero of the picture.

THE CREATURE (project-owned game art): the Loika the pod will become: a small round charcoal creature with a cream belly and muzzle, amber eyes, four stubby legs with pale toes and three green leaves on its head. Keep its design exactly; never invent another creature.

THE PAINTED LANGUAGE (one of our signed Vivarium room paintings, project-owned): its matte painterly miniature rendering, soft occlusion, warm golden light, cosy palette. Take the treatment and the warmth only, none of its objects.
prompt:
Paint the WHOLE screen of a cosy handheld creature-keeping game, 16:9, a calm front-on view slightly from above: the READING ROOM, where the player studies a pod (a wild seed pod with a creature's genome sleeping inside it) one page at a time. A naturalist at home after dark, one find on the table.
PLACEMENT (follow the layout): a plain dark slate band (#1d232b) across the very top and one across the very bottom, empty. Between them the wall behind, and a wooden study table whose top runs across the screen from a little above the middle down to the bottom band. A low small brass lamp hangs DIRECTLY above the pod, its shade just above the pod's cap; its warm pool of light falls on the pod. The POD stands on a low turned wooden dish with a thin brass lip, its centre a little left of the screen's centre (at about 39 percent of the width), in the pool; the pod is SMALL and modest, a little SHORTER than the creature beside it (the pod with its cap about 30 percent of the screen's height, the dish's foot at about 63 percent of the height), with a wide margin of wall above its cap; it is the brightest thing on screen, not the biggest. It is OUR pod, not a jar or vase: keep its round coral cap, its pale vertical ribs, its coral dots and its slate-blue colour; only its shell between the ribs is a translucent smoky slate-blue glass lit from within. The CREATURE stands on the table to the pod's right, at the pool's edge, about as tall as the pod. Top left, pinned to the wall: a small photo print of the place it was found (a meadow by a pond) on kraft paper with a blank strip under it, and below it a small kraft slip with a tiny painted pod on it (its kin). Top right, pinned: a small cream card with a tiny painting of a Loika with pale patches on its back (the player's goal). The lower part of the table (below the dish and the creature) is plain, quiet, empty wood, darker toward the bottom: nothing stands there (the game places its buttons and words there later). 
DIRECTION: THE BELL JAR. The pod stands under a clear glass bell jar with a small brass knob on top, the bell resting on the turned wooden dish with a brass rim. The lamp hangs a little to the left, so the bell throws a soft golden caustic of light onto the table. What is inside the pod is seen through two layers of glass (the bell, then the pod's own thin glassy shell between its ribs), which makes it feel further in and precious, a specimen in a naturalist's study. Keep the bell slender, clean and low-key so it never reads as a cage and never outshines the pod: the pod stays the brightest thing. Pinned papers are kraft and cream with brass pins.
STATE: A POD KNOWN IN FULL. The pod is now clear and still: its glass between the ribs is clean and quiet, holding only a calm steady glow, no motes left in it. The CREATURE stands whole beside it in its full colours, lit warmly, every part painted (charcoal with russet on the back, pale patches, cream belly, amber eyes, green leaves). On the front of the dish, a round wax stamp of warm honey-amber beeswax (not red) has just been pressed, with the small creature's head silhouette pressed into it and an irregular swollen edge: known in full. Under the creature, a few small painted tiles of its looks lie neatly in a short row. Contentment, a finished study.
LIGHT AND FINISH: one warm key light from the lamp, warm bounce, soft ambient occlusion, a soft contact shadow under every object. Matte, hand-painted miniature finish like the painted reference, cosy and warm, real depth; low saturation everywhere except the pod's inner light. No gloss, no chrome, no plastic, no neon, no sci-fi interface, no holograms, nothing childish.
NO text, letters, digits, numbers or logos anywhere, and no symbols other than the faint part silhouettes inside the pod (the game types its words later): the papers carry only their small paintings, with no writing. No buttons, no plates, no dishes other than the pod's one dish. No frame, no border, no vignette; the screen fills the canvas edge to edge.
